travel_rules: Hand luggage: liquids, gels, pastes and spreads in containers of 100 ml or less, all in one clear 1 L bag. Some airports have relaxed this, but this list follows the strict rule.
Japan does not let travellers bring in meat or meat products (including jerky, sausages and ham) without an export inspection certificate, which shops do not provide.
Food for personal use and gifts is duty-free in Japan within the overall allowance of 200,000 JPY per traveller.

souvenirs.name: Fazer Blue (Fazerin Sininen)

customs.note: Chocolate and sweets are not subject to animal or plant quarantine.

souvenirs.packing_tips: Melts in heat; keep it in the middle of the bag, not an outer pocket.
souvenirs.made_from: Sugar, whole milk powder, cocoa butter, cocoa mass
souvenirs.how_made: Milk chocolate made to Fazer's 1922 recipe, sold in the same blue wrapper since then.
souvenirs.taste: Sweet, creamy and milky, with a soft cocoa flavour.
souvenirs.where_to_buy: Any supermarket or kiosk; larger gift boxes at the Fazer café and the airport
souvenirs.tips: Both sources say every Finn they know brings this abroad as a gift.

souvenirs.name: Salty liquorice (salmiakki)

customs.note: Sweets are not subject to animal or plant quarantine.

souvenirs.how_made: Liquorice candy flavoured with ammonium chloride (*salmiakki*), which gives it a salty, tongue-tingling bite.
souvenirs.taste: Salty and bitter-sweet. Love it or hate it.
souvenirs.tips: A resident suggests giving it as a dare gift, with a sweeter chocolate next to it.

souvenirs.name: Rye crisps (ruislastut)

customs.note: Baked grain snacks are not subject to quarantine.

souvenirs.packing_tips: Crushes easily; pack it on top.
souvenirs.how_made: Thin slices of sour rye bread, baked or fried until crunchy and seasoned.
souvenirs.where_to_buy: Any supermarket, in the crisps aisle

souvenirs.name: Juhla Mokka coffee

customs.note: Roasted coffee is not subject to plant quarantine.

souvenirs.packing_tips: Some airports screen powders separately; keep it easy to take out.
souvenirs.how_made: A light-roasted blend from Paulig's Helsinki roastery, ground for filter coffee.
souvenirs.taste: Mild and smooth, the way Finns drink their many daily cups.
souvenirs.tips: One traveller brought it for coffee-loving friends; Finns drink the most coffee per person in the world.

customs.note: Japan does not let travellers bring in meat products without an export inspection certificate, which shops do not provide.

left_out.name: Lingonberry jam (puolukkahillo)
left_out.reason: Sold in jars of about 400 g, over the 100 ml carry-on limit for gels and spreads.
